falsifier: Pre-registered in STEP 0 and honoured: 'if the read is refused, empty, or returns data that is not Bastrop's, STOP and report. Do not build a bridge to a source that does not answer.' It FIRED, and the lane responded by narrowing scope rather than by building anyway: the v1 REST leg (bastrop.opengov.com /api/v1/entities and /reports) answered 200 with a 32-record global catalog of which ZERO are Bastrop's, and getReports() returns [] for Bastrop. So NO platform route was built on that leg. The BNP leg answered with Bastrop's own money and the bridge was built there. The falsifier was not merely declared; it changed the shape of what shipped.
contradicted: The dispatch's framing that 'Bastrop's finance data is wired in v1 and unreachable from v2' is TRUE, but the credential picture is not what the variable names say, and that is the one thing that would have broken the bridge silently. CP1 measured it: the key NAMED for BNP (smartcity-OPENGOV_BNP_API_KEY) returns 0 budgets for Bastrop, while the key named for the v1 REST API (smartcity-OPENGOV_API_KEY) returns all 12. Production works only because getBnpApiKey() reads OPENGOV_API_KEY FIRST. A lane that tidied that function to prefer its own namesake would have taken BNP to zero budgets and rendered UNACCOUNTED for a city whose budget is readable. Reported, not fixed: it is a credential-provisioning question, not a code change to make on a production service. SECOND CONTRADICTION, on the v2 side: permit revenue is not merely unreachable, it is WRONG at the source - measured live at a 150% collection rate - so the bridge carries a conflict rather than a clean number, which the dispatch did not anticipate. THIRD CONTRADICTION, found when STEP 2 ran: the dispatch's proof clause reads as though merging is most of the work and deploying is a formality ('read back services[0].source_commit_hash'). On this app, merging did not deploy anything at all - d12-main-uat has no deploy-on-push, and the previous deployment's cause was a manual spec update - so the proof required an explicit redeploy. A lane that had read the hash back the moment the PR merged would have read back the PREVIOUS commit and called it proof. The hash has to be read back AND compared against the merge commit, which is a different act from reading it.

LESSON: A helper that ends in `?? <some tenant>` cannot be used by any caller that REPORTS what it read. The fallback is invisible at the call site and the caller will publish a resolution that did not happen. Split the function: one that returns null, one that keeps the legacy default for existing callers.

Math.max(0, a - b) is a fabrication primitive. It converts an impossible state into a clean zero, and a clean zero is indistinguishable from a true zero downstream. Publish the signed difference and name the conflict.
Grep for the LITERAL misses the defaults that matter: one of the eight server.mjs fallbacks hides behind an imported DEFAULT_CITY_KEY. Enumerate by symbol and by literal.

A proof harness that boots the real routes beats a unit test for the answer direction, and it needs three things that are easy to forget: the vendor key in the environment, the OS trust store (--use-system-ca on a TLS-inspecting network, or Node reports a bare 'fetch failed'), and a dummy DATABASE_URL because server/db.ts throws on import without one.

Run the SAME probe against the OLD deployment before you deploy the new one. The window between 'merged' and 'deployed' is the only time a deployed paired control exists, and it is what turns 'the fix works' into 'the defect was here and now it is not' — on the surface, not in a runner. Miss the window and the pre-fix leg cannot be recovered by any amount of later testing.

A merge to main is not a deploy, and on d12-main-uat it is not even a trigger: the app has no deploy-on-push, so the merge produced no deployment and the previous one's cause was a manual UPDATE_SPEC. Read the previous deployment's `cause` before assuming a push deploys. apps-update with the spec returned unchanged plus update_all_source_versions: true is the documented way to redeploy from the tip, and SECRET env values round-trip in their existing EV[...] form.

A tenant-private pack is probed anonymously as its ACCESS answer, and that is not a wasted cell: 401 for bastrop_tx against 404 for a nonexistent pack proves the route resolved a real gated pack instead of folding it into the demo default. Say which refusal class each cell lands in; do not credential a probe until every cell returns 200, because that measures the credential and not the route.
DEAD_END: Do not build anything on bastrop.opengov.com /api/v1/entities or /reports: 200 with a 32-record catalog, zero of them Bastrop's, getReports() returning []. Tried, measured, rejected - and the rejection is why no route exists there.
Do not 'tidy' getBnpApiKey() to prefer OPENGOV_BNP_API_KEY. It reads OPENGOV_API_KEY first and that is the only reason BNP works.
Do not dedupe mygov_fees on your own judgement. The row count is real; which report window is authoritative is not a code question.
